suggested_french: J'ai un rendez-vous pour mon bilan annuel.
suggestion_note: One of the four EX44-EX47 rows whose v1 text is a bare noun phrase declared form=utterance, so it rendered as a fragment with no main clause. The fix is the one the speaker used: prefix a verb. v1's unhyphenated 'rendez vous' is normalised to 'rendez-vous' here and at EX46; PR07's sheet draft already had the hyphen, so v1 and the sheet disagreed with each other.

suggested_french: Je voudrais faire une analyse de sang.
suggestion_note: Same fragment fix. Third is applies=no, NO_RELATIONS: adult self-service, rule 12's beneficiary-equals-requester case.

suggested_french: J'ai un rendez-vous pour faire vacciner mon enfant.
suggestion_note: Rule 12: this is a SERVICE concept where the beneficiary and the requester differ, so the first person is the CARER who walks in, not the child. That is why rule 9's duplication test does not apply to it. PA10 collapsed into this concept; its French ('mon enfant doit recevoir ses vaccins') is reserved by the collapse ruling and the Kinyarwanda second_phrasing slot is empty, so nothing is proposed.

suggested_french: {REL} a un rendez-vous pour faire vacciner son enfant.
suggestion_note: ADULT_RELATIONS, and the group-A ruling working as intended: {REL} is the carer, the child stays LEXICAL as 'son enfant', no relation is a child and nothing goes circular. 'son enfant' is FR-2 and needs no gender ruling.

suggested_french: Je voudrais des conseils pour bien manger.
suggestion_note: Fragment fix, and the EX47 drift is closed rather than inherited. When the concept-drift survey ran, this row's Kinyarwanda had been rewritten to infant feeding — PR08's concept — and it has since been returned to 'Ndashaka inama ku mirire myiza.', general nutrition. The French follows the returned reading. Checked against PR08 and PR10, which are the other two advice requests: no union in either direction.

suggested_french: {REL} voudrait des conseils pour bien manger.
Quelqu'un a la maison a la tuberculose et je voudrais faire le test.
suggestion_note: FR-1: sheet draft D166's 'je veux etre depiste' is masculine, and the passive is what forces it, so the request is rephrased actively. PR01 IS ALSO THE PAIR THAT FALSIFIED A CLAIM IN THE CLOSURE DOC, and it does so in French too: its {REL} sits MID-PHRASE, so the first and third share a long leading run — 41 characters here — where docs/phrase-group-closure.md argues a prefix rule 'can never catch a first/third pair, because a third-person phrase begins with {REL}'. That held while every {REL} was sentence-initial and it no longer does. Harmless: the two persons of one concept are declared into one group anyway.

suggested_french: Quelqu'un a la maison a la tuberculose et {REL} voudrait faire le test.
suggestion_note: {REL} is mid-phrase here, so lint's rule-2 positional check will warn that it is not at the head. It is still the grammatical subject of its clause, which is what rule 2 is about; the warning is the heuristic's known weakness and the Kinyarwanda third has the identical shape.

OUT OF GENERATION, not merely held, and deliberately NOT applies=no. The concept is waiting on a Rwandan service-design ruling about whether men present for family planning. applies=no would record a settled answer where there is an open question, and would move the resolved count. Nothing is drafted. Sheet draft D168's text is recorded as dropped by the builder.
Third is additionally pinned 'NONE — do not generate' in routine_relation_sets.csv.

suggested_french: {REL} voudrait faire un test de depistage du VIH.

suggested_french: Je suis enceinte et je voudrais faire ma premiere consultation prenatale.
suggestion_note: Sheet draft D174 was only 'ma premiere consultation prenatale' and dropped the pregnancy, which the speaker's 'Ndatwite kandi ndashaka kwisuzumisha kwa muganga bwa mbere.' states first. Restored. 'enceinte' HAS NO MASCULINE and that is correct here, not an FR-1 defect: this is the one place in the corpus where the speaker's gender is known. PR05 is why the FR-1 exemption is keyed on the relation set as well as the domain — it is a PREVENTIVE concept ruled OBSTETRIC_RELATIONS, so a domain-only exemption would have flagged this row.

suggested_french: {REL} est enceinte et voudrait faire sa premiere consultation prenatale.
suggestion_note: OBSTETRIC_RELATIONS by an explicit ruling, so without it this preventive row would take the domain default of all eight and generate 'Mon mari est enceinte'. The set is uniformly feminine once 'Ma voisine' resolves the neighbour, which is what makes 'enceinte' safe across all four expansions.

suggested_french: Je voudrais faire verifier ma tension.
suggestion_note: Third is applies=no. PR06 was the last relation-ruling gap on the Kinyarwanda side and it resolved to NO_RELATIONS, superseding an earlier prose line that said adult relations.

suggested_french: Je voudrais faire le depistage du cancer du col de l'uterus.
suggestion_note: THE SHORT FORM IS KEPT, AND FRENCH INHERITS NONE OF THE CONSTRAINT THAT PRODUCED IT. The speaker wrote 'Ndashaka kwisuzumisha kanseri y'inkondo y'umura' rather than the longer 'go to the doctor to be checked for X' frame, because that frame shares 40 characters with CC09 and CC10 and would have grouped all three. The French 'je voudrais venir pour...' frame does NOT group them — measured, no union in either direction — so the short form here is a register choice rather than a forced one. It is also the better register, so nothing is lost by matching the speaker.

suggested_french: Je voudrais des conseils sur l'alimentation de mon jeune enfant.
suggestion_note: Rule 12: beneficiary and requester differ, so first person is the carer.

suggested_french: {REL} voudrait des conseils sur l'alimentation de son jeune enfant.
suggestion_note: ADULT_RELATIONS, group A. The child stays lexical.

suggested_french: Je voudrais un vermifuge pour mon enfant.
suggestion_note: ONE PLACE FRENCH IS SIMPLY UNPROBLEMATIC, recorded because most of this arm's notes run the other way. The Kinyarwanda needs a disambiguator here: 'inzoka' means both snake and worm, and this row uses the possessive to force the worm reading where HT07 used the verb '-rumwe'. 'Vermifuge' has no such ambiguity and needs no work.

suggested_french: {REL} voudrait un vermifuge pour son enfant.
suggestion_note: ADULT_RELATIONS. 'Ma grand-mere voudrait un vermifuge pour son enfant' is the presentation the set was widened to include — though see the flag list: whether the grandmother's 'son enfant' reads as her grandchild is a question for a French speaker, and the Kinyarwanda has 'umwana we' doing the same work.

suggested_french: Je voudrais des conseils pour rendre l'eau de boisson potable.
{REL} voudrait des conseils pour rendre l'eau de boisson potable.
suggestion_note: HOUSEHOLD_RELATIONS, group D. English says 'their drinking water' and French says 'l'eau de boisson' with no possessive at all, which is the natural form and sidesteps the question English had to answer.
